title: How high can a mountain be?
body: The rocks at the base of a mountain carry the weight of all the material above them. For a mountain of height h made of rock of density rho, the force per unit area at the base is about h rho g. The sides of a mountain are free, so this is not a case of uniform (bulk) compression; there is a shearing component of roughly h rho g itself. If this stress exceeds the elastic limit of the rock, the rock at the base begins to flow and the mountain cannot grow taller. For typical rock the elastic limit is about 30 × 10^7 N m^-2 and the density is about 3 × 10^3 kg m^-3. On Earth, with g = 10 m s^-2, equating h rho g to the elastic limit gives h = 10 km, which is a little more than the height of Mount Everest.
